0.0.n: Describes 仕事 as burdensome rather than physically heavy.

0.1.n: Refers to the task the speaker is considering asking someone to do.

0.2.n: Marks the resulting state with なる: becoming a demanding job.

0.3.n: Casual contraction of なってしまう, suggesting an unwelcome or burdensome outcome.

0.4.n: Softens the request by acknowledging that the task will be demanding.

0.6.n: The しよう form of お願いする expresses an intention being considered, softened by かな.

0.7.n: Combines with な to express uncertainty rather than ask a direct question.

0.8.n: Completes かな, giving the speaker's thought a reflective, tentative tone.

1.0.n: An enthusiastic, polite response accepting the request.

1.2.n: Polite form of 頑張る, used here as a promise of effort.

2.0.n: Modifies 社会人 to indicate someone just starting working life.

2.1.n: Usually refers to someone who has entered working life, often after finishing school.

2.3.n: The family name of the character 飯沼琴子.

2.4.n: The given name of the character 飯沼琴子.

2.5.n: Connects Kotoko's name to the title phrase that follows.

2.6.n: Describes こと positively as part of the title.

2.7.n: Refers broadly to experiences or happenings, not necessarily physical objects.

2.8.n: This is the first part of ランウェイ, an English borrowing; it is not a separate word here.

2.9.n: Completes ランウェイ, which forms part of the title.

3.0.n: Introduces the actor playing the lead role.

3.2.n: The family name of actor 畑芽育.

3.3.n: 芽 is the first character of the given name 芽育, read together as Mei.

3.4.n: 育 completes the given name 芽育; it is not a separate name here.

0.lit: It will end up becoming a demanding job, but I wonder if I'll ask you?
0.tip: しようかな expresses tentative intention: the speaker is considering asking, rather than directly requesting yet.

1.lit: Yes! I will do my best!
1.tip: 頑張ります is a polite way to promise effort when accepting a task.

2.lit: Newcomer working adult Iinuma Kotoko's good things runway.
2.tip: This is a title, so it names the show without needing a sentence-ending verb.

3.tip: Japanese names normally put the family name first: 畑 is the surname, and 芽育 is the given name.
